exposure: rate of weight gain during the second and third trimester of pregnancy, categorized according to IOM recommendations
outcome: poor neonatal outcome (severe neonatal morbidity or death)
cohort: 1569 pregnant women with singleton live births in rural Matlab, Bangladesh
finding: Gaining weight at rates below or above the IOM recommendations was associated with higher odds of several adverse perinatal outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, small- and large-for-gestational-age newborns, and poor neonatal outcome.
